correctness.rationale: The one-sided chain rule gives orbitwise cancellation by applying it to f^q=id. Conversely, on a chosen q-cycle the recursion λ_{i+1}=γ_i λ_i closes exactly when the γ product is one. A common factor P^(−1/q) on the first cycle preserves its ratios and changes the product of all λ values from P to one. Propagating positive slopes around the circle is then consistent even at the cut, and normalizing their integral gives a degree-one PL homeomorphism H. The conjugate f=HRH⁻¹ has J_f(H(y))=J_H(Ry)/J_H(y); off the union of selected cycles both factors are one, and on it the quotient is the prescribed γ. This includes nonunit support at precisely the selected positions, with positions understood in the rotation coordinate, not prescribed independently in physical space. A populated orbit needs at least two nonunit jumps and has at most q; every such size is attained by using r−1 jumps of 2 and one of 2^(1−r). Summing K sizes gives the entire interval 2K,…,qK. Twos and threes give every n≥2 for q≥3; q=2 gives only positive even totals. The omitted zero-break case is the rigid rotation. For the unrestricted necessity statement, an orientation-preserving finite-order circle map fixing a point is the identity (otherwise it moves monotonically under iteration on a cut interval). Thus every point of an order-q map has least period q.
residual_risks: The recorded 641 checks concern finite rational cyclic algebra; the normalized step function and arbitrary real positive jumps are established by the analytic proof, not by that script.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Applying the given-map theorem requires f already to have the specified jumps and orbit positions. originality.rationale: The supported distinction is inverse realization for arbitrary orbit-coordinate jump data, together with exact support. The product-one invariant and the finite-jump construction for the conjugating map are known and credited. The closest prior conjugacy theorem is an iff for a map already specified; it does not construct a map with arbitrary given orbit data. No equivalent inverse statement was located in the inspected sources.
residual_risks: The construction is short and could occur implicitly in other work on PL conjugacy or cyclic cohomology. The checked sources do not establish historical priority; the first cited paper is stronger than necessity alone for a map already given.

value.rationale: This answers a natural inverse question raised by the known cancellation condition: are there extra global constraints when exact break supports and all jump sizes on disjoint cycles are specified? Removing the distinct global compatibility obstruction without changing any prescribed quotient gives a family of exact witnesses for every allowed data set. It proves the sufficiency and sharp count spectrum, not just a new derivation of a necessary invariant or a check of a few low periods.
residual_risks: The value is for rotation coordinates only; there is no arbitrary physical-position interpolation claim.
